grounding.excerpt: (2) Perform WET testing at first discharge.

rationale: The permit's operative Part I clause explicitly requires WET testing at first discharge, establishing event-triggered (not routine monthly DMR) monitoring for parameter WET. The co-located Ceriodaphnia dubia reporting line in the same section specifies a Once/5 years frequency, consistent with special WET monitoring rather than a monthly numeric DMR limit. No packet evidence establishes WET as a monthly DMR numeric limit; the affirmative first-discharge trigger meets the burden to accept the event-triggered special-monitoring characterization.
